literal: Medicine as will not be needed for the body, if one eats after carefully ensuring that what was previously eaten has been digested.
translation: No medicine is needed for the body if one eats only after ensuring that what was previously consumed has been fully digested.
modern: முன் உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை உறுதி செய்து கொண்டு அதன் பிறகு உண்டால், உடம்பிற்கு மருந்து என்று ஒன்று தேவையில்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights a fundamental principle of preventive health. It states that the human body does not require any external medicine if a person regulates their eating habits. The key is to wait until the previously consumed food ('aruntiyatu') is completely digested ('aṟṟatu') before eating again. By carefully observing this digestion process ('pōṟṟi') and eating only when the body is ready ('uṇiṉ'), one maintains natural health, making medicine ('maruntu') entirely unnecessary.
